question: A client who must avoid bending after hip surgery asks how to dress the lower body independently. Which teaching is correct?
option_a: Sit on the edge of the bed, bend forward at the waist, and pull socks on quickly to limit time in flexion
option_b: Use a sock aid and a long-handled reacher or shoehorn while seated in a chair with the back supported, so the hip stays within flexion precautions
option_c: Stand and balance on the unoperated leg while lifting the operated foot to the knee to put on socks
option_d: Ask family members to dress the client completely until the surgical precautions end
correct_answer_text: Use a sock aid and a long-handled reacher or shoehorn while seated in a chair with the back supported, so the hip stays within flexion precautions
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Assistive Devices

question: A client reports leaking a small amount of urine whenever she coughs, laughs, or lifts her grandchild, but she never has a sudden urge to void and never leaks at night. Which type of incontinence does this pattern describe?
option_a: Urge incontinence, because leakage is involuntary
option_b: Stress incontinence: leakage with increased abdominal pressure, without a preceding urge
option_c: Overflow incontinence, because the bladder is not emptying
option_d: Functional incontinence, because she cannot reach the toilet in time
correct_answer_text: Stress incontinence: leakage with increased abdominal pressure, without a preceding urge
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Elimination

question: An immobile client has a heel wound completely covered by a dry, stable, intact eschar with no redness, drainage, or fluctuance. Which action is correct?
option_a: Soften the eschar with moisture and arrange for it to be debrided this shift
option_b: Document it as a stage 2 pressure injury
option_c: Leave the stable heel eschar in place as a natural protective cover, offload the heel completely, and monitor it closely for change
option_d: Apply firm massage over the eschar to improve circulation
correct_answer_text: Leave the stable heel eschar in place as a natural protective cover, offload the heel completely, and monitor it closely for change
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Mobility/Immobility

question: A client with severe peripheral arterial disease and Raynaud phenomenon sprains a wrist and asks the nurse to apply an ice pack. What is the nurse's best response?
option_a: Apply the ice for 30 minutes every hour as requested
option_b: Explain that cold is avoided with impaired circulation because vasoconstriction can worsen tissue ischemia, and offer an alternative comfort plan while notifying the provider of the injury
option_c: Alternate ice and heat every 10 minutes to balance the effects
option_d: Apply ice only to the fingers, away from the wrist
correct_answer_text: Explain that cold is avoided with impaired circulation because vasoconstriction can worsen tissue ischemia, and offer an alternative comfort plan while notifying the provider of the injury
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Nonpharmacological Comfort Interventions

question: An immobile older adult client has no fluid restriction and poor voluntary fluid intake. Which hydration plan should the nurse implement?
option_a: Offer fluids on a schedule throughout waking hours, keep a filled water container within the client's reach, and monitor intake, output, and mucous membranes
option_b: Wait until the client asks for fluids, because thirst is a reliable signal in older adults
option_c: Restrict evening fluids to reduce nighttime toileting without discussing it with the client
option_d: Provide one large container of water each morning and document the full amount as consumed
correct_answer_text: Offer fluids on a schedule throughout waking hours, keep a filled water container within the client's reach, and monitor intake, output, and mucous membranes
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Nutrition and Oral Hydration

question: A client who wears contact lenses has a red, painful eye with discharge and has continued wearing the lenses 'to see the whiteboard at work.' Which instruction is correct?
option_a: Continue wearing the lenses but add lubricating drops every hour
option_b: Switch to wearing the lenses only at night until the redness resolves
option_c: Remove the lenses now, do not reinsert them until the eye has been evaluated and cleared, wear glasses meanwhile, and discard or disinfect the lenses and case as directed because they may be contaminated
option_d: Rinse the lenses under tap water and store them in a cup of water overnight
correct_answer_text: Remove the lenses now, do not reinsert them until the eye has been evaluated and cleared, wear glasses meanwhile, and discard or disinfect the lenses and case as directed because they may be contaminated
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Personal Hygiene

question: A client at 32 weeks of gestation reports that she cannot get comfortable in bed and wakes with heartburn and backache. Which rest positioning teaching is most appropriate?
option_a: Sleep flat on her back with one thin pillow so the spine stays straight
option_b: Rest in a side-lying position (preferably the left side) with a pillow between the knees and support under the abdomen, and elevate the head of the bed slightly if heartburn is troublesome
option_c: Sleep prone with a pillow under the hips for the third trimester
option_d: Stay in bed on strict bed rest during the day so nighttime sleep improves
correct_answer_text: Rest in a side-lying position (preferably the left side) with a pillow between the knees and support under the abdomen, and elevate the head of the bed slightly if heartburn is troublesome
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Rest and Sleep

question: A sexually active 70-year-old widow with a new partner says she no longer needs condoms 'at my age.' Which teaching is correct?
option_a: She is correct — infection risk ends after menopause
option_b: Condoms are needed only if the partner is under 50
option_c: Pregnancy is no longer a concern, but condoms are still needed with a new partner because sexually transmitted infections occur at all ages and postmenopausal tissue changes can raise infection risk
option_d: A dental dam alone provides complete protection for all sexual activity
correct_answer_text: Pregnancy is no longer a concern, but condoms are still needed with a new partner because sexually transmitted infections occur at all ages and postmenopausal tissue changes can raise infection risk
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Aging Process

question: A client at 38 weeks asks how to perform fetal movement (kick) counts at home. Which instruction is correct?
option_a: Lie on your side at a time the baby is usually active and count movements; about 10 movements within up to 2 hours is reassuring, and clearly reduced movement should be reported promptly
option_b: Count only kicks hard enough to be seen through clothing, over a full 24 hours
option_c: Drink several caffeinated beverages first so the baby moves more
option_d: Counts are unnecessary in the last month because the baby has less room
correct_answer_text: Lie on your side at a time the baby is usually active and count movements; about 10 movements within up to 2 hours is reassuring, and clearly reduced movement should be reported promptly
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Ante-/Intra-/Postpartum and Newborn Care

question: A 26-year-old client says, 'My partner and I are building a life together, and that closeness matters more to me now than figuring out who I am was in school.' This best illustrates which developmental task?
option_a: Generativity versus stagnation (middle adulthood)
option_b: Intimacy versus isolation (young adulthood)
option_c: Identity versus role confusion (adolescence)
option_d: Ego integrity versus despair (older adulthood)
correct_answer_text: Intimacy versus isolation (young adulthood)
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Developmental Stages and Transitions

question: A parent asks when a healthy 8-month-old should receive the influenza vaccine. Which answer is correct?
option_a: Influenza vaccine is recommended every year for everyone 6 months of age and older, and young children receiving it for the first time need 2 doses that season, spaced at least 4 weeks apart
option_b: Influenza vaccine is not given until age 2 years
option_c: One dose in infancy protects for several years
option_d: Influenza vaccine is recommended only for children with asthma
correct_answer_text: Influenza vaccine is recommended every year for everyone 6 months of age and older, and young children receiving it for the first time need 2 doses that season, spaced at least 4 weeks apart
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Health Promotion/Disease Prevention

question: A client has office blood pressures of 142/88 and 144/90 mm Hg on two separate visits, confirmed with correct technique. How should the nurse explain this category?
option_a: These readings fall in the stage 2 hypertension range (at or above 140/90) and need provider-directed treatment planning, not just re-screening in a year
option_b: This is elevated blood pressure; recheck in 1 year
option_c: This is stage 1 hypertension; lifestyle changes alone are always sufficient
option_d: A single home reading below 120/80 would erase this classification
correct_answer_text: These readings fall in the stage 2 hypertension range (at or above 140/90) and need provider-directed treatment planning, not just re-screening in a year
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Health Screening

question: A parent discovers a 16-year-old has been texting while driving and asks the nurse for the most effective approach. Which advice is best?
option_a: Tell the teen that experienced drivers can text safely at red lights
option_b: Set a clear family rule with consequences, model phone-free driving, and use a phone setting/app that blocks notifications while the car is moving
option_c: Recommend texting only on straight roads
option_d: Suggest holding the phone higher so the teen's eyes stay near the road
correct_answer_text: Set a clear family rule with consequences, model phone-free driving, and use a phone setting/app that blocks notifications while the car is moving
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — High-Risk Behaviors

question: The parent of a 6-year-old with asthma smokes outside the home but drives the child to school in a car where smoking also occurs. Which teaching is most complete?
option_a: Smoking outside only is sufficient protection for the child
option_b: Make the home and car completely smoke-free, because smoke residue in the car still triggers asthma and smoking by a window or door does not protect the child
option_c: Smoking in the car is fine if the windows are fully open
option_d: Switching to vaping in the car eliminates the child's exposure
correct_answer_text: Make the home and car completely smoke-free, because smoke residue in the car still triggers asthma and smoking by a window or door does not protect the child
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Lifestyle Choices

question: A client with asthma has a written action plan using peak flow zones. The client is in the yellow zone with increased cough and wheeze but is speaking in full sentences. What does the plan direct?
option_a: Use the prescribed quick-relief inhaler and step-up medicines as written, then reassess and seek care if not improving
option_b: Stop all inhalers until the next office visit
option_c: Go immediately to call emergency services for any cough
option_d: Double the inhaled corticosteroid permanently without contacting the provider
correct_answer_text: Use the prescribed quick-relief inhaler and step-up medicines as written, then reassess and seek care if not improving
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Self-Care

question: A nurse is teaching new parents about the newborn metabolic screening (heel-stick) test. Which statement is accurate?
option_a: The test must be drawn before the infant's first feeding to be valid
option_b: A positive screen confirms the diagnosis of phenylketonuria
option_c: The screen is optional and rarely changes management
option_d: The screen is collected after 24 hours of age and after the infant has been fed, and a positive screen requires confirmatory testing
correct_answer_text: The screen is collected after 24 hours of age and after the infant has been fed, and a positive screen requires confirmatory testing
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Techniques of Physical Assessment

question: A competent client in a long-term care facility tells the nurse, 'I signed that directive years ago. I have changed my mind — I want full treatment now.' What should the nurse do?
option_a: Tell the client a signed directive can never be changed
option_b: Ask the family to vote on whether the change is genuine
option_c: File the request away until the client's next annual review
option_d: Notify the provider promptly, document the client's verbal revocation and new wishes, and make sure the whole team is informed
correct_answer_text: Notify the provider promptly, document the client's verbal revocation and new wishes, and make sure the whole team is informed
topic: Management of Care — Advance Directives/Self-Determination/Life Planning

question: At a care conference, the team is deciding a client's discharge destination. The client, who has capacity, has not been invited and has told the nurse she wants to go home with services. What is the nurse's best advocacy action?
option_a: Let the team decide and inform the client of the outcome afterward
option_b: Tell the client the team's decision is final and cannot be appealed
option_c: Ask the family to decide privately and report back to the team
option_d: Advocate for the client to participate in the conference, or to have her stated preference formally presented, before a destination is decided
correct_answer_text: Advocate for the client to participate in the conference, or to have her stated preference formally presented, before a destination is decided
topic: Management of Care — Advocacy

question: A new graduate RN in week 3 of orientation asks the charge nurse for the assignment with 'the sickest client, to learn faster.' Which response best applies assignment principles?
option_a: Assign clients matched to the new graduate's validated competencies with preceptor support, increasing complexity as competence is demonstrated
option_b: Grant the request, because motivation is the best predictor of safe practice
option_c: Assign the new graduate only clients who need no medications for the whole orientation
option_d: Let the new graduate choose any assignment, since the preceptor can intervene if needed
correct_answer_text: Assign clients matched to the new graduate's validated competencies with preceptor support, increasing complexity as competence is demonstrated
topic: Management of Care — Assignment, Delegation and Supervision

question: A client no longer meets criteria for acute hospital care. The family says they are 'not ready' for the client to move to a skilled nursing facility. What is the case manager's best approach?
option_a: Explain the options and the appeal/notice process, explore the family's specific concerns, and facilitate a timely, safe transition to the appropriate level of care
option_b: Keep the client in the acute bed indefinitely without further discussion
option_c: Discharge the client home without services to resolve the disagreement
option_d: Tell the family the hospital will bill them personally starting today as a penalty
correct_answer_text: Explain the options and the appeal/notice process, explore the family's specific concerns, and facilitate a timely, safe transition to the appropriate level of care
topic: Management of Care — Case Management

question: A client refuses a recommended blood draw, saying, 'No more needles today.' The nurse believes the result is important for the provider's decisions. What is the nurse's best response?
option_a: Draw the blood while the client is sleeping so the refusal does not delay care
option_b: Respect the refusal, explain what information the test would provide and the possible consequences of skipping it, document the informed refusal, and notify the provider
option_c: Ask the client's spouse to sign permission for the draw instead
option_d: Tell the client refusing a test means the client will be discharged
correct_answer_text: Respect the refusal, explain what information the test would provide and the possible consequences of skipping it, document the informed refusal, and notify the provider
topic: Management of Care — Client Rights

question: At interdisciplinary rounds, a client ready for discharge in 2 days still lacks a walker, home oxygen approval, and medication reconciliation. What is the nurse's best contribution?
option_a: Note the barriers in the chart and let the discharge day team handle them
option_b: Coordinate with physical therapy, case management, respiratory services, and pharmacy today so each barrier is resolved before discharge
option_c: Tell the family to purchase the equipment privately to avoid delays
option_d: Recommend delaying discharge by a week without contacting other services
correct_answer_text: Coordinate with physical therapy, case management, respiratory services, and pharmacy today so each barrier is resolved before discharge
topic: Management of Care — Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team

question: A 36-bed unit sets a nurse-to-client ratio of 1:4 for the day shift. How many RNs must be scheduled to meet the ratio for a full census of 36 clients?
option_a: 8 RNs, because one nurse can cover the charge role as well
option_b: 12 RNs, calculated as 36 divided by 3
option_c: 6 RNs, because support staff make up the difference
option_d: 9 RNs, calculated as 36 clients divided by 4 clients per nurse
correct_answer_text: 9 RNs, calculated as 36 clients divided by 4 clients per nurse
topic: Management of Care — Concepts of Management

question: A man telephones the unit saying he is a client's husband and asking for her test results. The nurse does not recognize his voice and the client is asleep. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Give the results, since spouses are entitled to them
option_b: Verify the caller's identity and the client's permission/release preferences through the facility process before disclosing any information
option_c: Confirm only whether the client is a patient, and give results if he insists
option_d: Read the results to him if he can state the client's date of birth
correct_answer_text: Verify the caller's identity and the client's permission/release preferences through the facility process before disclosing any information
topic: Management of Care — Confidentiality/Information Security

question: A client is discharged while a biopsy result is still pending. Which action best protects continuity of care?
option_a: Leave the pending result out of the discharge paperwork since it is not back yet
option_b: Keep the client in the hospital for several more days solely to wait for the result
option_c: Document the pending result, the provider responsible for acting on it, and the follow-up contact plan, and communicate all three to the client and the receiving provider
option_d: Tell the client that results pending at discharge no longer matter
correct_answer_text: Document the pending result, the provider responsible for acting on it, and the follow-up contact plan, and communicate all three to the client and the receiving provider
topic: Management of Care — Continuity of Care

question: A clinic nurse takes a phone call from a client who says, 'My words are coming out wrong and my right side feels weak — it started about 20 minutes ago.' What is the nurse's best action?
option_a: Tell the client to rest and call back if symptoms persist another hour
option_b: Schedule the client for the first available appointment tomorrow
option_c: Ask the client to drive himself to the clinic for evaluation
option_d: Direct the client (or a bystander) to call emergency services now for immediate stroke evaluation and stay on the line as appropriate
correct_answer_text: Direct the client (or a bystander) to call emergency services now for immediate stroke evaluation and stay on the line as appropriate
topic: Management of Care — Establishing Priorities

question: A nurse repeatedly experiences moral distress when assigned to cases where the plan of care conflicts with the nurse's values, and is beginning to dread coming to work. What is the most appropriate action?
option_a: Request an ethics consultation or debriefing and raise the concern through the unit's established channels
option_b: Refuse all assignments without notice until the schedule changes
option_c: Document the nurse's personal objections to the family in the client's chart
option_d: Discourage the family from visiting so the conflict is less visible
correct_answer_text: Request an ethics consultation or debriefing and raise the concern through the unit's established channels
topic: Management of Care — Ethical Practice

question: A nurse scans a medication and the system displays a hard-stop alert: the scanned product is a look-alike package of a different strength than ordered. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Stop, return the product, obtain the correct strength, and rescan — treating the alert as a safety barrier that caught a real error
option_b: Override the alert, because the packages look nearly identical
option_c: Give the medication and document that the alert was probably a system error
option_d: Ask a coworker to scan a different package so the alert clears
correct_answer_text: Stop, return the product, obtain the correct strength, and rescan — treating the alert as a safety barrier that caught a real error
topic: Management of Care — Information Technology

question: A 16-year-old who lives independently, is self-supporting, and is legally emancipated needs a procedure. Who provides consent?
option_a: The emancipated minor provides their own consent
option_b: Both parents must provide consent regardless of emancipation
option_c: The provider consents on the minor's behalf
option_d: A court order is required for every procedure
correct_answer_text: The emancipated minor provides their own consent
topic: Management of Care — Informed Consent

question: Which chart entry is legally sound documentation of a client's agitated behavior?
option_a: Chart personal labels such as 'the client is a manipulative liar' so the next nurse is warned
option_b: Chart objective observations and the client's own words, such as pacing, raised voice, and a quoted statement, with times and interventions
option_c: Omit the episode from the record entirely to protect the client
option_d: Share the nurse's opinions about the client verbally at handoff but write nothing
correct_answer_text: Chart objective observations and the client's own words, such as pacing, raised voice, and a quoted statement, with times and interventions
topic: Management of Care — Legal Rights and Responsibilities

question: After a unit introduces a new barcode medication process, a nurse notices workarounds that bypass scanning when the unit is busy. What is the best action?
option_a: Report the pattern through the safety and performance improvement process so workflow causes can be addressed
option_b: Use the workaround as well, since experienced staff find it faster
option_c: Confront each nurse individually and threaten discipline
option_d: Wait for an error to occur before raising the concern
correct_answer_text: Report the pattern through the safety and performance improvement process so workflow causes can be addressed
topic: Management of Care — Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement)

question: A client in intensive care is being evaluated for brain death after a catastrophic injury. What is the nurse's appropriate role regarding organ donation?
option_a: Ask the family at the bedside whether they want to donate organs before any evaluation is complete
option_b: Ensure timely referral to the organ procurement organization per policy and support the family, leaving the donation discussion to designated, trained requestors
option_c: Decide independently that donation is inappropriate and withhold the referral
option_d: Tell the family that donation will delay all end-of-life care by several days
correct_answer_text: Ensure timely referral to the organ procurement organization per policy and support the family, leaving the donation discussion to designated, trained requestors
topic: Management of Care — Referrals

question: A client taking semaglutide for type 2 diabetes reports severe, persistent abdominal pain that radiates to the back, with vomiting. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Reassure the client that severe back-radiating pain is an expected effect that passes in a few weeks
option_b: Advise the client to take the next dose with a large fatty meal to slow absorption
option_c: Instruct the client to hold the medication and notify the prescriber promptly for possible pancreatitis
option_d: Suggest an over-the-counter antacid and reassessment at the next annual visit
correct_answer_text: Instruct the client to hold the medication and notify the prescriber promptly for possible pancreatitis
topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — Adverse Effects/Contraindications/Side Effects/Interactions

question: The blood bank calls to say a unit of packed red blood cells is ready, but the nurse cannot begin the transfusion for 50 minutes. What is the correct action?
option_a: Pick up the unit now and keep it at the nurses' station so it is ready when needed
option_b: Pick up the unit now and store it in the unit medication refrigerator until the nurse is free
option_c: Start the unit in 50 minutes and run it over 6 hours to make up for the delay
option_d: Leave the unit at the blood bank until the transfusion can be started within 30 minutes of its release, and complete it within 4 hours once started
correct_answer_text: Leave the unit at the blood bank until the transfusion can be started within 30 minutes of its release, and complete it within 4 hours once started
topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — Blood and Blood Products

question: A nurse is removing a central venous catheter. Which technique is correct?
option_a: Sit the client upright at 90 degrees and have the client inhale deeply as the catheter is pulled
option_b: Place the client supine, have the client perform a Valsalva maneuver or hold the breath during removal, then apply pressure with an occlusive dressing
option_c: Remove the catheter quickly during inspiration with no dressing ready, then cover the site with dry gauze
option_d: Cut the catheter at the skin line and leave the internal portion in place
correct_answer_text: Place the client supine, have the client perform a Valsalva maneuver or hold the breath during removal, then apply pressure with an occlusive dressing
topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — Central Venous Access Devices

question: An insulin infusion bag contains 100 units of regular insulin in 100 mL of normal saline and is running at 8.5 mL/hr. How many units per hour is the client receiving?
option_a: 85 units/hr
option_b: 8.5 units/hr
option_c: 4.25 units/hr
option_d: 17 units/hr
correct_answer_text: 8.5 units/hr
topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — Dosage Calculations

question: A client with influenza started oseltamivir 30 hours after symptom onset. Which teaching reflects correct expectations for this therapy?
option_a: The medication cures influenza within 2 hours of the first dose
option_b: The medication works only if started within the first 6 hours, so it should be discarded now
option_c: Started within about 48 hours of symptom onset, it can shorten the illness and reduce complications, and the full prescribed course should be completed even as symptoms improve
option_d: The client should also take a leftover antibiotic to make the antiviral work
correct_answer_text: Started within about 48 hours of symptom onset, it can shorten the illness and reduce complications, and the full prescribed course should be completed even as symptoms improve
topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — Expected Actions/Outcomes

question: A client with asthma is prescribed a twice-daily inhaled corticosteroid. Which teaching best prevents the most common local adverse effect?
option_a: Use the rescue inhaler immediately after each corticosteroid dose
option_b: Hold the breath for 2 seconds only, then exhale through the nose
option_c: Take the dose on an empty stomach to improve absorption
option_d: Rinse the mouth with water and spit after each dose
correct_answer_text: Rinse the mouth with water and spit after each dose
topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — Medication Administration

question: A nurse assessing a peripheral IV site finds swelling, coolness, and pallor around the insertion site, and the infusion has slowed. The client reports tightness at the site. What is the nurse's best action?
option_a: Slow the infusion further and apply a warm compress, then reassess in 2 hours
option_b: Flush the line forcefully to restore the flow rate
option_c: Advance the catheter slightly to reposition the tip
option_d: Stop the infusion, remove the catheter, elevate the limb, and restart the IV in a different site
correct_answer_text: Stop the infusion, remove the catheter, elevate the limb, and restart the IV in a different site
topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — Parenteral/Intravenous Therapies

question: A client with a prior myocardial infarction 2 years ago asks to use celecoxib daily for knee osteoarthritis. Which teaching is most important?
option_a: Celecoxib has no cardiovascular risk because it spares the stomach
option_b: Take the highest dose available, because joint pain requires it
option_c: NSAIDs including celecoxib can increase the risk of heart attack and stroke, so the prescriber should weigh this history and use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time if it is chosen
option_d: Combine celecoxib with daily ibuprofen for added protection
correct_answer_text: NSAIDs including celecoxib can increase the risk of heart attack and stroke, so the prescriber should weigh this history and use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time if it is chosen
topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — Pharmacological Pain Management

question: A client on TPN develops a temperature of 101.9 F, chills, and redness at the central line site. Which action should the nurse take first?
option_a: Give an antipyretic and reassess at the end of the shift
option_b: Slow the TPN rate by half and continue monitoring
option_c: Remove the TPN and discard the line without cultures
option_d: Notify the prescriber, obtain cultures as ordered, and follow the line-infection protocol
correct_answer_text: Notify the prescriber, obtain cultures as ordered, and follow the line-infection protocol
topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — Total Parenteral Nutrition

question: A 4-week-old infant has forceful, projectile vomiting after feeds, is constantly hungry, and has lost weight. A small olive-shaped mass is palpated in the right upper abdomen. Which plan is most appropriate?
option_a: Keep the infant NPO, notify the provider, and anticipate intravenous fluids and electrolyte correction before pyloromyotomy
option_b: Feed smaller amounts more often and reassure the parents this is normal reflux
option_c: Switch to a soy formula and recheck weight in a month
option_d: Give an antiemetic and discharge the infant once vomiting stops for an hour
correct_answer_text: Keep the infant NPO, notify the provider, and anticipate intravenous fluids and electrolyte correction before pyloromyotomy
topic: Physiological Adaptation — Alterations in Body Systems

question: A client who took a large aspirin overdose has tinnitus and rapid, deep breathing. Arterial blood gases: pH 7.47, PaCO2 20 mm Hg, HCO3 14 mEq/L. Which interpretation is correct?
option_a: A normal blood gas for a client who is hyperventilating
option_b: Simple metabolic acidosis with full respiratory compensation
option_c: Simple acute respiratory alkalosis with normal renal compensation
option_d: A mixed disorder: primary respiratory alkalosis combined with a metabolic acidosis, the classic salicylate pattern
correct_answer_text: A mixed disorder: primary respiratory alkalosis combined with a metabolic acidosis, the classic salicylate pattern
topic: Physiological Adaptation — Fluid and Electrolyte Imbalances

question: A monitored client has HR 38, BP 86/52, dizziness, and chest discomfort unresponsive to atropine. What should the nurse prepare for next?
option_a: Oral metoprolol to slow the rate further
option_b: Defibrillation at the highest energy
option_c: Transcutaneous pacing with pads placed and sedation or analgesia as prescribed, while preparing for transvenous pacing if needed
option_d: Reassurance that bradycardia is always benign in older adults
correct_answer_text: Transcutaneous pacing with pads placed and sedation or analgesia as prescribed, while preparing for transvenous pacing if needed
topic: Physiological Adaptation — Hemodynamics

question: A client with diabetes reports early fullness, bloating, vomiting of food eaten hours earlier, and glucose readings that swing unpredictably after meals. Which plan best fits gastroparesis?
option_a: Three large meals with a high-fiber salad at each meal
option_b: Lying flat immediately after eating to aid digestion
option_c: Stopping all glucose monitoring because readings are unreliable
option_d: Small, frequent, low-fat, low-fiber meals, liquids or soft foods when symptoms flare, and glucose checks after meals because insulin timing may need prescriber adjustment
correct_answer_text: Small, frequent, low-fat, low-fiber meals, liquids or soft foods when symptoms flare, and glucose checks after meals because insulin timing may need prescriber adjustment
topic: Physiological Adaptation — Illness Management

question: A 24-year-old client reports sudden severe right-sided pelvic pain with nausea that began during exercise. The right ovary is exquisitely tender and ultrasound shows an enlarged ovary with reduced blood flow. Which interpretation and action are correct?
option_a: A urinary stone that can be managed with outpatient fluids
option_b: A ruptured simple cyst that will resolve with a heating pad and routine follow-up
option_c: Normal ovulation pain that needs no further assessment
option_d: Probable ovarian torsion cutting off the ovary's blood supply; notify the provider immediately because surgery is time-sensitive
correct_answer_text: Probable ovarian torsion cutting off the ovary's blood supply; notify the provider immediately because surgery is time-sensitive
topic: Physiological Adaptation — Medical Emergencies

question: A client with sepsis is oozing blood from IV sites and gums while also developing mottled, cool fingers. Labs show low platelets, prolonged clotting times, low fibrinogen, and elevated fibrin degradation products. Which mechanism explains bleeding and clotting occurring together?
option_a: Disseminated intravascular coagulation: widespread clot formation consumes platelets and clotting factors, leaving too few for normal hemostasis
option_b: The liver has stopped making vitamin K, so only bleeding should occur
option_c: The bone marrow has stopped producing red blood cells
option_d: Heparin in the IV flush has dissolved all of the body's fibrinogen
correct_answer_text: Disseminated intravascular coagulation: widespread clot formation consumes platelets and clotting factors, leaving too few for normal hemostasis
topic: Physiological Adaptation — Pathophysiology

question: A client taking lithium for years develops a coarse hand tremor, unsteady gait, and slurred speech during a week of gastroenteritis with poor intake, while also taking a thiazide diuretic. Which action is most appropriate?
option_a: Hold the lithium pending prescriber direction, notify the provider of probable toxicity, assess hydration and sodium, and anticipate IV fluids
option_b: Give an extra lithium dose because the tremor means levels are low
option_c: Encourage a low-salt diet to reduce the tremor
option_d: Advise the client to wait until the next routine level in 3 months
correct_answer_text: Hold the lithium pending prescriber direction, notify the provider of probable toxicity, assess hydration and sodium, and anticipate IV fluids
topic: Physiological Adaptation — Unexpected Response to Therapies

question: A nurse in the emergency department treats a toddler with a spiral femur fracture. The accompanying adult's explanation changes between staff members and does not match the injury pattern for a non-ambulatory child. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Document objective findings, follow mandated reporting for suspected abuse, and avoid accusing the adult during care
option_b: Discharge the child once the fracture is stabilized because reporting is optional
option_c: Tell the adult the story is not believable and refuse further care until police arrive
option_d: Ask the adult to demonstrate how the injury happened using the child
correct_answer_text: Document objective findings, follow mandated reporting for suspected abuse, and avoid accusing the adult during care
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Abuse or Neglect

question: A client on an inpatient unit repeatedly demands exceptions (extra phone time, special meals) and becomes tearful, saying, "You'd do it if you cared," when refused by some staff but has received exceptions from others. Which intervention is most effective?
option_a: Grant exceptions when the client is tearful to avoid escalating the situation
option_b: Rotate staff daily so no single nurse has to enforce the limits repeatedly
option_c: Explain to the client that demanding behavior is a character flaw the team cannot reward
option_d: Apply one written, team-agreed set of limits consistently, stated calmly each time, without debating the client's motives
correct_answer_text: Apply one written, team-agreed set of limits consistently, stated calmly each time, without debating the client's motives
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Behavioral Interventions

question: A client who snorted cocaine 40 minutes ago reports crushing chest pain. Findings: BP 178/104 mm Hg, pulse 124/min, temperature 100.9 F (38.3 C), agitation and profuse sweating. Which action is the priority?
option_a: Give a beta blocker first to bring the heart rate down quickly
option_b: Encourage the client to walk the hallway to burn off the drug's energy
option_c: Treat as a cardiac emergency: continuous monitoring, notify the provider, and anticipate a benzodiazepine and nitroglycerin per protocol while avoiding beta-blocker-only treatment
option_d: Discharge once the pain eases, because pain in a young user is usually anxiety
correct_answer_text: Treat as a cardiac emergency: continuous monitoring, notify the provider, and anticipate a benzodiazepine and nitroglycerin per protocol while avoiding beta-blocker-only treatment
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Chemical and Other Dependencies/Substance Use Disorder

question: An 8-year-old who had surgery 2 days ago has begun wetting the bed and asking for a baby bottle, although she was fully toilet trained and drank from a cup before admission. Which nursing response to the parents is most appropriate?
option_a: Explain that she is manipulating them and advise them to ignore the babyish behavior
option_b: Suggest they scold her gently so she returns to age-appropriate behavior before discharge
option_c: Explain that temporary regression is common in hospitalized school-age children, respond calmly and matter-of-factly, and expect the behavior to fade as she recovers
option_d: Restrict visitors so she learns to manage the hospital stay independently
correct_answer_text: Explain that temporary regression is common in hospitalized school-age children, respond calmly and matter-of-factly, and expect the behavior to fade as she recovers
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Coping Mechanisms

question: A client who survived an assault 5 days ago cannot sleep, replays the event, and says, 'I keep thinking I should have fought harder.' Which intervention is most appropriate in this early phase?
option_a: Have her recount the assault in full detail repeatedly until it becomes less upsetting
option_b: Normalize the reactions, reduce self-blame, assess safety and support, and connect her with trauma-informed resources
option_c: Tell her self-blame means she is developing a long-term disorder
option_d: Advise her to make major life decisions quickly so she regains control
correct_answer_text: Normalize the reactions, reduce self-blame, assess safety and support, and connect her with trauma-informed resources
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Crisis Intervention

question: A competent adult client who is a Jehovah's Witness needs surgery with a moderate bleeding risk and clearly declines allogeneic blood transfusion, asking about alternatives. Which action is most appropriate?
option_a: Ask the client's spouse to sign consent for transfusion in case it is needed
option_b: Tell the client the surgery cannot be done at any facility without transfusion consent
option_c: Document 'noncompliant with recommended care' and proceed with routine orders
option_d: Honor and document the refusal, notify the surgeon and anesthesia team, and collaborate on a blood-conservation plan (for example, cell salvage or erythropoietin where appropriate)
correct_answer_text: Honor and document the refusal, notify the surgeon and anesthesia team, and collaborate on a blood-conservation plan (for example, cell salvage or erythropoietin where appropriate)
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Cultural Awareness/Cultural Influences on Health

question: A client with end-stage heart failure enrolled in hospice tells the nurse, "I know I am not getting better. I want to stay home and be comfortable." The client's daughter asks the nurse to hide the prognosis from her mother. What is the nurse's best response?
option_a: Agree to the daughter's request to protect the client from distress
option_b: Tell the daughter the client has a right to decide, then change the subject
option_c: Support the client's expressed wishes, facilitate a family conversation about goals of care, and notify the hospice team
option_d: Ask the provider to remove hospice services until the family agrees
correct_answer_text: Support the client's expressed wishes, facilitate a family conversation about goals of care, and notify the hospice team
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — End-of-Life Care

question: After a client's stroke, his wife has taken over finances, medications, and all decisions; the client, who can communicate, sits silently during visits and has stopped attempting tasks he can still do. Which nursing action best addresses this family dynamic?
option_a: Praise the wife for taking charge so the client can rest completely
option_b: Tell the wife she is causing the client's dependence and must step back entirely
option_c: Direct all questions to the wife since she manages his care
option_d: Assess what tasks the client can safely do and coach the couple on supported independence with shared decision-making
correct_answer_text: Assess what tasks the client can safely do and coach the couple on supported independence with shared decision-making
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Family Dynamics

question: A 14-year-old whose mother died 4 months ago is brought to the clinic for recurrent stomachaches with no medical cause found. His grades have fallen, he has quit the soccer team, and he tells the nurse, 'Dad cries if I talk about Mom, so I just don't.' Which action is most appropriate?
option_a: Recognize that adolescents often grieve through physical complaints, withdrawal, and protecting a grieving parent; explore his grief with him and arrange grief support for both the adolescent and his father
option_b: Reassure the father that stomachaches at this age are always attention-seeking and need no follow-up
option_c: Advise the adolescent to talk to his father nightly about his mother so the father gets used to it
option_d: Document normal grief and advise the family to return in a year if symptoms persist
correct_answer_text: Recognize that adolescents often grieve through physical complaints, withdrawal, and protecting a grieving parent; explore his grief with him and arrange grief support for both the adolescent and his father
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Grief and Loss

question: A client with obsessive-compulsive disorder spends 40 minutes washing hands before meals and becomes panicked if interrupted. Which intervention is most appropriate initially?
option_a: Block the sink area at mealtimes so the client is forced to skip the ritual
option_b: Explain once that the germs fear is irrational and expect the ritual to stop
option_c: Allow the ritual on a negotiated schedule while gradually building agreed limits and response-prevention practice with the treatment team
option_d: Complete the handwashing for the client so meals are not delayed
correct_answer_text: Allow the ritual on a negotiated schedule while gradually building agreed limits and response-prevention practice with the treatment team
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Mental Health Concepts

question: A client asks the nurse, 'Will you pray aloud with me before my surgery?' The nurse does not share the client's faith tradition and feels uncomfortable leading the prayer. Which action is most appropriate?
option_a: Decline and leave the room promptly so the client can pray alone
option_b: "I can sit with you while you pray, and I can also call the chaplain or your own faith leader right now — which would you prefer?"
option_c: Lead the prayer using wording from the nurse's own tradition, since any prayer should comfort the client
option_d: Tell the client that staff are not permitted to be present during religious practices
correct_answer_text: "I can sit with you while you pray, and I can also call the chaplain or your own faith leader right now — which would you prefer?"
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Religious and Spiritual Influences on Health

question: A client with severe vision loss from advanced glaucoma reports seeing vivid, detailed images of flowers and faces that she knows are not real. She is alert, oriented, and distressed, asking, 'Am I losing my mind?' Which action is most appropriate?
option_a: Document probable new psychosis and request antipsychotic medication
option_b: Tell her the images are a normal part of aging and require no follow-up
option_c: Reassure her that vivid visual experiences with preserved insight occur in severe vision loss, assess her safety and eye status, and notify the provider for evaluation
option_d: Advise her to keep the images secret, because reporting them will lead to a psychiatric hold
correct_answer_text: Reassure her that vivid visual experiences with preserved insight occur in severe vision loss, assess her safety and eye status, and notify the provider for evaluation
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Sensory/Perceptual Alterations

question: A client with chronic tension headaches asks the nurse to teach a stress-management technique that can be used at work. Which teaching is most appropriate?
option_a: Advise the client to take extra breaks by leaving work early each day
option_b: Teach slow diaphragmatic breathing with brief practice and instructions to use it at headache onset
option_c: Recommend the client avoid all stressful assignments permanently
option_d: Suggest vigorous exercise during the headache to release tension
correct_answer_text: Teach slow diaphragmatic breathing with brief practice and instructions to use it at headache onset
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Stress Management

question: A client recovering from a first episode of psychosis is being discharged to live alone and says, "I do not know anyone here and I stop going to appointments when I feel alone." Which discharge action best addresses this concern?
option_a: Provide only the clinic phone number and advise calling if needed
option_b: Delay discharge indefinitely until the client makes friends
option_c: Connect the client before discharge with a peer support program and community mental-health follow-up, and confirm the first appointment
option_d: Tell the client that independence requires managing without support
correct_answer_text: Connect the client before discharge with a peer support program and community mental-health follow-up, and confirm the first appointment
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Support Systems

question: A teenage client admitted after an overdose has sat with arms crossed, answering every question with "fine." Which approach is most therapeutic?
option_a: "You need to talk if you want us to be able to help you."
option_b: "Your parents are worried sick; don't you think you owe them an explanation?"
option_c: "I'll ask the questions and you just nod yes or no until you cooperate."
option_d: "It's okay if talking is hard right now. I'll sit with you a while, and you can tell me things at your pace."
correct_answer_text: "It's okay if talking is hard right now. I'll sit with you a while, and you can tell me things at your pace."
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Therapeutic Communication

question: On an inpatient unit, a client who was pacing and shouting now picks up a chair and moves toward another client while threatening to hit them. Staff attempts at verbal de-escalation have failed. What is the most appropriate next action?
option_a: Ask other clients to restrain the client while staff leave to get help
option_b: Offer the client a snack and suggest discussing the conflict tomorrow
option_c: Document the behavior and continue routine observation
option_d: Initiate the facility's emergency response for imminent danger, which may include seclusion or restraint per protocol, with continuous monitoring
correct_answer_text: Initiate the facility's emergency response for imminent danger, which may include seclusion or restraint per protocol, with continuous monitoring
topic: Psychosocial Integrity — Therapeutic Environment

question: During assessment of a client with an irregular rhythm, the apical pulse is 96/min while the radial pulse is 78/min. How should the nurse interpret and act on this?
option_a: There is a pulse deficit of 18 beats/min, meaning not every heartbeat perfuses the wrist; count the apical rate for a full minute, document both rates, and report the deficit
option_b: The radial rate is the accurate one and the apical count can be discarded
option_c: A deficit under 20 beats/min is always a normal finding
option_d: Recheck only if the client develops chest pain next week
correct_answer_text: There is a pulse deficit of 18 beats/min, meaning not every heartbeat perfuses the wrist; count the apical rate for a full minute, document both rates, and report the deficit
topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — Changes/Abnormalities in Vital Signs

question: A client is scheduled for a small-bowel capsule endoscopy. Which preparation and post-procedure points are correct?
option_a: The client may eat a full breakfast, because the capsule camera works around food
option_b: The client fasts as directed before swallowing the capsule, wears the recording device for about 8 hours, and checks stools for passage of the capsule, reporting if it is not seen or if abdominal pain or vomiting occurs
option_c: The client will be sedated for the entire study and must arrange a driver
option_d: The capsule dissolves in the stomach, so no passage check is needed
correct_answer_text: The client fasts as directed before swallowing the capsule, wears the recording device for about 8 hours, and checks stools for passage of the capsule, reporting if it is not seen or if abdominal pain or vomiting occurs
topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — Diagnostic Tests

question: A 71-year-old client reports a new one-sided headache, scalp tenderness when brushing her hair, and pain in her jaw after chewing for a few minutes. Results: erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 94 mm/hr, C-reactive protein markedly elevated. Which action is most appropriate?
option_a: Reassure the client that a high ESR is nonspecific and recheck it at her annual visit
option_b: Advise her to take an over-the-counter analgesic and return if the headache lasts another month
option_c: Document the results as consistent with tension headache and schedule routine follow-up
option_d: Notify the provider promptly today: this symptom pattern with markedly elevated inflammatory markers raises concern for giant cell (temporal) arteritis, which threatens vision and needs urgent evaluation
correct_answer_text: Notify the provider promptly today: this symptom pattern with markedly elevated inflammatory markers raises concern for giant cell (temporal) arteritis, which threatens vision and needs urgent evaluation
topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — Laboratory Values

question: A client with known adrenal insufficiency is admitted with gastroenteritis and has BP 86/52 mm Hg, pulse 118/min, sodium 128 mEq/L, potassium 5.6 mEq/L, and glucose 58 mg/dL. Which action is the priority?
option_a: Anticipate immediate stress-dose IV glucocorticoid (such as hydrocortisone) and isotonic fluids with dextrose; this pattern is an adrenal crisis precipitated by illness
option_b: Give insulin to correct the potassium before any other treatment
option_c: Restrict fluids because the sodium is low
option_d: Schedule an outpatient endocrine referral for next month
correct_answer_text: Anticipate immediate stress-dose IV glucocorticoid (such as hydrocortisone) and isotonic fluids with dextrose; this pattern is an adrenal crisis precipitated by illness
topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — Potential for Alterations in Body Systems

question: The day after cataract surgery, a client reports sudden severe pain in the operated eye, nausea, and a marked decrease in vision, and the eye looks red. Which action is most appropriate?
option_a: Notify the surgeon immediately, because severe pain with nausea and vision loss can signal a pressure rise or bleeding inside the eye
option_b: Reassure the client that this degree of pain is expected and offer acetaminophen
option_c: Apply a warm compress to the eye for comfort
option_d: Remove the eye shield and have the client rub the eye gently
correct_answer_text: Notify the surgeon immediately, because severe pain with nausea and vision loss can signal a pressure rise or bleeding inside the eye
topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — Potential for Complications from Surgical Procedures and Health Alterations

question: Shortly after a thoracentesis that removed 1,600 mL of pleural fluid, a client develops a persistent cough, worsening dyspnea, and pink frothy sputum with SpO2 90%. Which complication should the nurse suspect?
option_a: An anxiety response to the procedure that will settle with reassurance
option_b: A tension pneumothorax on the opposite side
option_c: Fluid overload caused by the intravenous fluids given during the procedure
option_d: Re-expansion pulmonary edema in the lung that was rapidly re-inflated after large-volume fluid removal
correct_answer_text: Re-expansion pulmonary edema in the lung that was rapidly re-inflated after large-volume fluid removal
topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — Potential for Complications of Diagnostic Tests/Treatments/Procedures

question: After a head injury, a client responds to painful stimulation with both arms extended, turned inward and pronated, legs extended, and feet plantar-flexed. Which interpretation is correct?
option_a: This is seizure activity that should be timed but not reported
option_b: This is decorticate (flexor) posturing, the most severe motor response
option_c: This is a normal withdrawal reflex to pain
option_d: This is decerebrate (extensor) posturing, indicating brainstem-level dysfunction that is more ominous than flexor posturing and requires urgent notification
correct_answer_text: This is decerebrate (extensor) posturing, indicating brainstem-level dysfunction that is more ominous than flexor posturing and requires urgent notification
topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — System-Specific Assessments

question: A client with a nasogastric tube for decompression after bowel surgery has had no output for 3 hours, reports increasing nausea, and the abdomen is more distended. Which action should the nurse take first?
option_a: Give an oral antiemetic through the tube
option_b: Remove the tube because it is no longer working
option_c: Assess tube placement and patency per protocol, including checking for kinks and irrigating only as ordered
option_d: Advance the tube 5 cm to reach pooled fluid
correct_answer_text: Assess tube placement and patency per protocol, including checking for kinks and irrigating only as ordered
topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — Therapeutic Procedures

question: A nurse collects a wound culture specimen and is called away before labeling it. Where and when should the container be labeled?
option_a: At the nurses' station once all specimens from the unit are gathered
option_b: At the client's bedside, immediately after collection, in the client's presence, before leaving the room
option_c: In the laboratory drop-off area, using the printed requisition stack
option_d: By the nursing assistant during the next specimen transport run
correct_answer_text: At the client's bedside, immediately after collection, in the client's presence, before leaving the room
topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Accident/Error/Injury Prevention

question: Immediately after an earthquake, a nurse's unit has ceiling tiles down in one corridor, a strong gas odor near the utility room, and several clients with minor injuries. What is the nurse's best action?
option_a: Use the elevator to move all clients to the lobby at once
option_b: Assess clients for injuries, avoid the hazardous corridor, report conditions and hazards to the incident command structure, and prepare clients for possible evacuation by stairs per direction
option_c: Send staff back into the damaged corridor to retrieve supplies
option_d: Discharge all ambulatory clients out the main entrance immediately on the nurse's own authority
correct_answer_text: Assess clients for injuries, avoid the hazardous corridor, report conditions and hazards to the incident command structure, and prepare clients for possible evacuation by stairs per direction
topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Emergency Response Plan

question: A nurse must move several heavy cases of IV fluid from a delivery pallet to the supply room. Which approach follows ergonomic principles?
option_a: Carry two cases at a time against the chest to halve the trips
option_b: Load the cases onto a cart and make trips rather than carrying them, keeping any single lifted load close to the body with the legs doing the lifting
option_c: Stack the cases and lift the stack from the floor with a straight back bend at the waist
option_d: Ask one coworker to toss each case while the nurse catches and shelves it
correct_answer_text: Load the cases onto a cart and make trips rather than carrying them, keeping any single lifted load close to the body with the legs doing the lifting
topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Ergonomic Principles

question: A nurse finds an unlabeled spray bottle of cleaning solution in a client's bathroom left by housekeeping. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Smell the contents to identify the cleaner
option_b: Remove it from use and notify housekeeping/supervisor; secondary containers must be labeled with the product identity and hazard warnings
option_c: Use it anyway because housekeeping products are all the same
option_d: Pour it into a labeled bottle so it can stay in the room
correct_answer_text: Remove it from use and notify housekeeping/supervisor; secondary containers must be labeled with the product identity and hazard warnings
topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Handling Hazardous and Infectious Materials

question: A family plans to use a portable generator during a power outage. Which instruction is most important?
option_a: Run it in the garage with the garage door cracked open for ventilation
option_b: Run it on the covered porch so rain cannot reach it
option_c: Run the generator outdoors, at least 20 feet (about 6 m) from the home, with the exhaust directed away from windows and doors
option_d: Run it in the basement near a small window that can be opened
correct_answer_text: Run the generator outdoors, at least 20 feet (about 6 m) from the home, with the exhaust directed away from windows and doors
topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Home Safety

question: A nurse realizes an hour later that a medication administration was never charted. How should the entry be made in the electronic record?
option_a: Make a late entry now that is clearly identified as a late entry, recording the actual administration time and the time of charting, without altering any existing entry
option_b: Backdate the entry to the administration time without noting it is late
option_c: Ask a coworker who was present to enter it under the coworker's login
option_d: Delete the scheduled dose and re-enter it as given now
correct_answer_text: Make a late entry now that is clearly identified as a late entry, recording the actual administration time and the time of charting, without altering any existing entry
topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Reporting of Incident/Event/Irregular Occurrence/Variance

question: A nurse finds an enteral feeding tube connector that could be attached to an IV line by mistake. Which safeguard prevents this misconnection error?
option_a: Use enteral-specific (ENFit) connectors and tubing that are physically incompatible with IV ports, and trace the line from the feeding bag to the client before starting
option_b: Tape the feeding tubing to the IV tubing so both stay organized together
option_c: Use an IV syringe to flush the feeding tube because it fits well
option_d: Label the feeding bag but keep standard Luer connectors on all lines
correct_answer_text: Use enteral-specific (ENFit) connectors and tubing that are physically incompatible with IV ports, and trace the line from the feeding bag to the client before starting
topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Safe Use of Equipment

question: A man whose employment ended last month presents at a staff entrance and asks a nurse to badge him in, saying his old badge 'stopped working' and he left personal items in a locker. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Badge him in, because retrieving personal property is harmless
option_b: Hold the door while he walks to the locker room and back
option_c: Ask him to wait outside and bring his items out without checking his status
option_d: Decline to badge him in, direct him to the security desk to verify his status and arrange an escorted retrieval if authorized, and notify security
correct_answer_text: Decline to badge him in, direct him to the security desk to verify his status and arrange an escorted retrieval if authorized, and notify security
topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Security Plan

question: A nurse gives an intramuscular injection using a needle with an hinged safety shield. When should the safety device be activated?
option_a: Immediately after withdrawing the needle, before the needle is placed in the sharps container
option_b: At the end of the shift, when all used needles are collected
option_c: Before the injection, so the shield is ready while the drug is given
option_d: Only if the needle will be carried to a sharps container in another room
correct_answer_text: Immediately after withdrawing the needle, before the needle is placed in the sharps container
topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Standard Precautions/Transmission-Based Precautions/Surgical Asepsis

question: A provider writes an order for a wrist restraint 'as needed whenever the client becomes restless.' Why must the nurse question this order?
option_a: Restraints may not be ordered on an as-needed (PRN) basis; each use requires an order based on the client's current behavior and clinical justification
option_b: Restraints can only be ordered by a nurse practitioner
option_c: Wrist restraints are prohibited in all circumstances
option_d: The order is acceptable if the nurse documents restlessness each time
correct_answer_text: Restraints may not be ordered on an as-needed (PRN) basis; each use requires an order based on the client's current behavior and clinical justification
topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Use of Restraints/Safety Devices

question: A client recovering from hip surgery will bathe at home and must not flex the operated hip beyond 90 degrees. Which home bathing equipment plan is most appropriate?
option_a: A raised toilet seat and a shower chair with a hand-held shower, so the client can sit without deep hip flexion
option_b: A low bathtub bench placed at the bottom of the tub so the client sits with knees fully bent
option_c: No equipment, because sitting on the regular toilet and tub floor is good exercise for the new hip
option_d: A standard stool in the shower with no back and no hand supports
correct_answer_text: A raised toilet seat and a shower chair with a hand-held shower, so the client can sit without deep hip flexion
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Assistive Devices

question: A nurse is preparing to administer a prescribed cleansing enema to an adult client. Which positioning and technique are correct?
option_a: Place the client prone and raise the solution container as high as possible for rapid flow
option_b: Place the client in the right lateral position so the solution follows the ascending colon
option_c: Insert the tube toward the sacrum at a downward angle to enter the rectum
option_d: Place the client in the left lateral (Sims) position with the right knee flexed, and hang the container a moderate height above the anus so the solution flows by gravity into the descending colon
correct_answer_text: Place the client in the left lateral (Sims) position with the right knee flexed, and hang the container a moderate height above the anus so the solution flows by gravity into the descending colon
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Elimination

question: A client is 1 day post total hip arthroplasty through a posterior approach. Which instruction set is correct for this client?
option_a: Cross the legs at the ankles to keep the new joint stable
option_b: Use an abduction pillow, do not flex the hip beyond 90 degrees, and do not cross the legs or turn the operated leg inward
option_c: Flex the hip fully when sitting to prevent stiffness
option_d: Sleep on the operated side with the legs tightly together
correct_answer_text: Use an abduction pillow, do not flex the hip beyond 90 degrees, and do not cross the legs or turn the operated leg inward
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Mobility/Immobility

question: A client sprained an ankle 3 hours ago; it is swollen and painful. Which comfort intervention is most appropriate at this stage?
option_a: Apply a warm compress to increase blood flow to the joint
option_b: Encourage the client to walk on the ankle to prevent stiffness
option_c: Apply a cold pack with a barrier for limited intervals and elevate the ankle above heart level
option_d: Wrap the ankle loosely only at night so swelling can resolve on its own
correct_answer_text: Apply a cold pack with a barrier for limited intervals and elevate the ankle above heart level
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Nonpharmacological Comfort Interventions

question: A nurse is inserting a nasogastric tube. Which positioning and maneuver best facilitate safe passage?
option_a: Sit the client in high-Fowler position, then have the client flex the neck with chin toward the chest and sip water or swallow as the tube advances
option_b: Lay the client flat with the neck hyperextended backward during the whole insertion
option_c: Have the client tilt the head back and hold the breath until the tube reaches the stomach
option_d: Insert the tube while the client is lying on the left side with legs extended
correct_answer_text: Sit the client in high-Fowler position, then have the client flex the neck with chin toward the chest and sip water or swallow as the tube advances
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Nutrition and Oral Hydration

question: A nurse provides eye care for a client with bacterial conjunctivitis in the right eye. Which technique is correct?
option_a: Clean from the outer canthus inward to push debris toward the tear duct
option_b: Use the same cloth section for both eyes to save supplies
option_c: Irrigate the affected eye toward the unaffected eye across the nose
option_d: Clean from the inner canthus outward with a separate clean section of cloth for each wipe, and care for the unaffected eye first or with separate supplies
correct_answer_text: Clean from the inner canthus outward with a separate clean section of cloth for each wipe, and care for the unaffected eye first or with separate supplies
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Personal Hygiene

question: An older adult tells the nurse, "I wake up at 4 a.m. and cannot get back to sleep, so I must need a sleeping pill." Which response best reflects normal aging sleep changes and appropriate guidance?
option_a: Agree that early waking always indicates a disorder requiring medication
option_b: Explain that sleep becomes lighter with more awakenings with age, and suggest reviewing caffeine, naps, and evening routines before considering medication
option_c: Advise staying in bed awake until normal waking time no matter what
option_d: Recommend doubling evening exercise right before bed to force deeper sleep
correct_answer_text: Explain that sleep becomes lighter with more awakenings with age, and suggest reviewing caffeine, naps, and evening routines before considering medication
topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Rest and Sleep

question: During a January home visit, a 79-year-old living alone keeps the house at 60 F (15.5 C) to save money and wears a light sweater. Which teaching addresses the aging-related risk?
option_a: Reassure the client that feeling comfortable means body temperature is safe
option_b: Explain that aging reduces shivering and blood-vessel responses to cold, so older adults can become hypothermic indoors; the home should be kept at a safe warmth (at least about 68 F / 20 C) with layered clothing and blankets
option_c: Recommend a hot bath each evening as the main warming strategy
option_d: Suggest drinking a glass of alcohol before bed to improve circulation
correct_answer_text: Explain that aging reduces shivering and blood-vessel responses to cold, so older adults can become hypothermic indoors; the home should be kept at a safe warmth (at least about 68 F / 20 C) with layered clothing and blankets
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Aging Process

question: A client asks about the timing of routine postpartum follow-up care. Which explanation follows current obstetric guidance?
option_a: Contact with the care team within the first 3 weeks after birth, with a comprehensive visit no later than 12 weeks, and earlier or more frequent contact for complications
option_b: A single visit at 6 months is sufficient for all clients
option_c: No follow-up is needed if the birth was uncomplicated and the client feels well
option_d: Follow-up is only for the newborn; the birthing parent needs none in the first year
correct_answer_text: Contact with the care team within the first 3 weeks after birth, with a comprehensive visit no later than 12 weeks, and earlier or more frequent contact for complications
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Ante-/Intra-/Postpartum and Newborn Care

question: A 4-year-old tells the nurse, 'I got sick because I was bad and didn't listen.' What is the nurse's best response?
option_a: Agree that behaving better will prevent future illness, to motivate good behavior
option_b: Ignore the comment and change the subject to the child's toys
option_c: Tell the child that only doctors can explain why people get sick
option_d: Gently explain that illness is caused by germs and body problems, not by being bad, and that nothing the child did caused the sickness
correct_answer_text: Gently explain that illness is caused by germs and body problems, not by being bad, and that nothing the child did caused the sickness
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Developmental Stages and Transitions

question: Parents ask about the meningococcal (MenACWY) vaccine schedule for their healthy 11-year-old. Which information is correct?
option_a: A single dose at age 11 protects for life with no booster
option_b: The series is given in infancy along with the other 2-month vaccines
option_c: The first dose is routinely given at 11 to 12 years, with a booster at 16 years
option_d: Vaccination is recommended only for college freshmen
correct_answer_text: The first dose is routinely given at 11 to 12 years, with a booster at 16 years
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Health Promotion/Disease Prevention

question: A 45-year-old client who has never been screened asks about hepatitis C testing. Which statement is correct?
option_a: Testing is offered only to clients who report injection drug use
option_b: Hepatitis C cannot be treated, so screening is not useful
option_c: At least one hepatitis C screening test is recommended for all adults ages 18 to 79, with repeat testing for ongoing risk
option_d: Screening is done with a yearly liver ultrasound instead of a blood test
correct_answer_text: At least one hepatitis C screening test is recommended for all adults ages 18 to 79, with repeat testing for ongoing risk
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Health Screening

question: A 17-year-old who vapes daily says, 'At least it is not smoking, so my lungs are fine.' Which response best addresses the risk?
option_a: Explain that vaping still delivers addictive nicotine that affects the developing adolescent brain and exposes the lungs to harmful aerosols, and offer cessation resources/quit support
option_b: Agree that vaping is harmless for teenagers
option_c: Recommend switching to menthol cigarettes as a step down
option_d: Tell the teen that willpower alone is the only accepted method
correct_answer_text: Explain that vaping still delivers addictive nicotine that affects the developing adolescent brain and exposes the lungs to harmful aerosols, and offer cessation resources/quit support
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — High-Risk Behaviors

question: A 16-year-old athlete drinks two large energy drinks daily before practice and reports a racing heartbeat and poor sleep. Which teaching is correct?
option_a: Energy drinks are equivalent to sports drinks and are safe before practice
option_b: The racing heartbeat is a normal training effect unrelated to the drinks
option_c: Energy drinks deliver high doses of caffeine and sugar that can cause palpitations, anxiety, and sleep disruption, and they are not recommended for adolescents or as sports hydration
option_d: Switching to coffee before practice removes the caffeine concern
correct_answer_text: Energy drinks deliver high doses of caffeine and sugar that can cause palpitations, anxiety, and sleep disruption, and they are not recommended for adolescents or as sports hydration
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Lifestyle Choices

question: A client with diabetes asks about daily foot care. Which statement by the client shows correct understanding?
option_a: I should walk barefoot at home to toughen my feet
option_b: I should soak my feet in hot water every evening
option_c: I can trim calluses with a razor when they get thick
option_d: I will inspect my feet daily, wash with lukewarm water, moisturize the tops and soles but not between the toes, and never walk barefoot
correct_answer_text: I will inspect my feet daily, wash with lukewarm water, moisturize the tops and soles but not between the toes, and never walk barefoot
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Self-Care

question: A nurse will perform an otoscopic examination on a 2-year-old. Which technique is correct for this age?
option_a: Pull the pinna up and back, as for an adult
option_b: Insert the speculum as deeply as possible to see the membrane
option_c: Ask the child to hold the otoscope steady
option_d: Pull the pinna down and back to straighten the canal, use the largest speculum that fits comfortably, and brace the otoscope against the child's head
correct_answer_text: Pull the pinna down and back to straighten the canal, use the largest speculum that fits comfortably, and brace the otoscope against the child's head
topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Techniques of Physical Assessment

question: A client with a serious mental illness, currently stable and competent, tells the nurse: 'When I am in a crisis I refuse one particular medication because of how it affected me, but I do want hospital care.' Which tool best records these future preferences?
option_a: A do-not-resuscitate order, which the provider can write today based on the client's statement
option_b: A note asking the family to remember the preference and explain it during any crisis
option_c: A financial power of attorney naming a relative to manage the client's hospital bills
option_d: A psychiatric advance directive, in which the client states treatment preferences and may name an agent for future periods of incapacity
correct_answer_text: A psychiatric advance directive, in which the client states treatment preferences and may name an agent for future periods of incapacity
topic: Management of Care — Advance Directives/Self-Determination/Life Planning

question: During an adolescent's clinic visit, the client asks for a few minutes alone with the nurse to discuss a sensitive health concern. The parent insists on staying for the entire visit. What is the nurse's best action?
option_a: Refuse the request, since parents must be present for everything
option_b: Promise the adolescent absolute secrecy regardless of any safety concern disclosed
option_c: Record the private conversation and send the parent a transcript
option_d: Provide a brief private interview as part of the visit, explaining to both parties the confidentiality protections and their safety-related limits
correct_answer_text: Provide a brief private interview as part of the visit, explaining to both parties the confidentiality protections and their safety-related limits
topic: Management of Care — Advocacy

question: A licensed practical nurse (LPN) working under an RN's direction says, 'The provider just gave me a telephone order to change the IV rate on an unstable client — I will enter it and adjust the pump.' What is the RN's best action?
option_a: Let the LPN proceed, because telephone orders may be taken by any licensed nurse
option_b: Ask the LPN to have a UAP witness the pump change instead
option_c: Tell the LPN to wait until the end of the shift when the RN has more time
